title: Introduce startup hedge, fast failstop and ghost-connection pruner
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Adds a startup hedging layer to prevent global cold-start cascades.
- Adds a fast failstop to hard-fail noisy long-poll connections during node startup.
- Introduces a background ghost-connection pruner to reclaim leaked sockets.
- Default behaviour is conservative; operators should validate via canary before wide rollout.
description:
Background: during a late-night incident we observed a pattern where large numbers of long-lived client connections opened during node bootstrapping would stall scheduling, causing subsequent requests to pile up and SLOs to degrade. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) a startup-hedge admission layer that applies a temporary admission window during node warmup, prioritizing short/fast requests and applying soft token limits for bursty opens, (2) a fast failstop that proactively terminates connections that exceed a short startup-specific stall threshold (this prevents a single slow peer from blocking scheduler hot paths), and (3) a ghost-connection pruner that scans and reclaims sockets which are locally leaked or orphaned after process handoffs.

What changed (summary):
- Implemented startup_hedge.go: configurable warmup window, request scoring, and a per-node transient token pool.
- Added failstop.go: low-latency detection + termination path with metrics and audit logging.
- Added ghost_pruner.go: background sweeper with non-blocking checks and safe reclamation hooks.
- Tied the hedging and failstop into the main connection orchestrator (cmd/agent/main.go).
- Added end-to-end tests that simulate large connection churn during node restart.
- Added operational runbook (internal/sre/runbooks/startup-hedge.md) and metrics to telemetry config.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for heuristic logic and edge cases
- [x] E2E sim to reproduce prior incident class
- [x] Runbook with rollback steps and canary guidance
- [x] Telemetry (histograms and counters) for alerting
- [x] Feature gate so behavior is opt-in in release branch

Commits: ["impl: startup hedge admission and token pool", "feat: fast failstop for startup stalls", "fix: ghost pruner safety checks and race fix", "test: add e2e churn scenario and unit coverage", "docs: add runbook and telemetry notes"]

Files changed (high level): ["go/pkg/scheduler/startup_hedge.go", "go/pkg/scheduler/failstop.go", "go/pkg/network/ghost_pruner.go", "cmd/agent/main.go", "internal/sre/runbooks/startup-hedge.md", "pkg/telemetry/metrics.yaml", "tests/e2e/startup-hedge.test", "Dockerfile"]

Testing & CI: initial CI run revealed a race in ghost_pruner when running with the e2e harness (flaky coverage on Linux M1 runners). I pushed a small synchronization fix and re-ran the CI. Final status: all unit, integration and e2e checks passed. CI artifacts and flamegraphs are attached to the run.

Performance/Cost: the hedging layer introduces negligible CPU overhead (checked under load: <2% median CPU increase at 95th percentile) and reduces tail latency under bootstrap churn by ~45% in our lab. The ghost pruner runs with a low-frequency default (every 30s) and uses a non-blocking scanner to avoid impacting hot paths.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind startup_hedge_v1; canary on dedicated-capacity region eu-west-1 for 24h with telemetry thresholds: request P99 latency, scheduler queue depth, and socket FD pressure. If any metric regresses >10% for 15 minutes, the operator should flip the gate off (runbook contains exact commands).

Migration notes: no DB schema changes. For Private customers with strict networking, the runbook includes an optional step to coordinate agent restarts.

Related work: ENG-8765 (engineering spec), SRE-112 (post-incident), SUP-4012 (customer report incident).

Merge: squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI. Backport to release/2026.02 will be submitted as a separate PR if canary is successful.
